families.apiFamily: Module system, createRequire, dynamic require, and package subpaths
families.acceptedSemantics: The agent embed bundle has a manifest-owned dynamic require allowlist and createRequire returns that bundle-local require shim. Unknown dynamic require throws a typed BrainkitUnsupportedDynamicRequireError.
knownGaps: No filesystem-aware Node module resolver exists inside QuickJS.
User package deployment does not inherit agent embed package patches or arbitrary npm resolution.
Dynamic import remains bundle/profile-specific rather than a full Node loader.
families.nextProof: Gate 8 must make source package bare npm imports fail with a resolver-profile diagnostic instead of a generic esbuild error.

families.apiFamily: process metadata, env, cwd, argv, versions, nextTick, and stdio shape
families.acceptedSemantics: Process metadata and env are provided for package feature detection and runtime configuration. nextTick is supported for package scheduling.
knownGaps: Process exit and process mutation APIs are not runtime control surfaces.
Node reports, inspector, and low-level process handles are not supported.
families.nextProof: Keep unavailable process mutators documented and covered by typed unsupported tests when packages reach them.

families.apiFamily: timers, promises, microtasks, async_hooks, and AsyncLocalStorage
families.acceptedSemantics: Timers and timer promises are usable. AsyncLocalStorage supports synchronous run/enterWith/disable nesting, AsyncResource snapshot capture/runInAsyncScope, and store propagation across Brainkit-owned callback boundaries: setTimeout, setInterval, setImmediate, queueMicrotask, timersPromises callback chains, fetch promise callbacks returned by jsbridge fetch, EventEmitter-based stream/http callbacks, JS runtime bus.subscribe handlers, and bus.callStream onChunk/final promise callbacks.
knownGaps: AsyncLocalStorage does not provide general Promise-hook propagation or preserve context across arbitrary await chains.
createHook does not provide global async resource instrumentation.
executionAsyncId and triggerAsyncId are shape values.
families.nextProof: Keep arbitrary Promise propagation explicitly unsupported until real async-hook semantics exist; add integration proof if future bus surfaces introduce new Go-scheduled callback paths.

families.apiFamily: Node streams, Web Streams, EventEmitter, pipeline, finished, and async iteration
families.acceptedSemantics: Web Streams are the preferred streaming primitive. Node stream compatibility covers package interop, event delivery, pipe-like data flow, and async iteration used by current dependencies.
knownGaps: Full Node backpressure and internal readable/writable state are not promised.
stream/promises remains shape/minimal until direct canaries require pipeline or finished semantics.
families.nextProof: Gate 7 should add a readable-stream canary and promote stream/promises only after focused pipeline/finished tests exist.

families.apiFamily: Buffer, text encoding, base64, binary crossings, and string decoding
families.acceptedSemantics: The Buffer and encoding APIs needed by current bundle dependencies are supported directly by jsbridge.
knownGaps: Future binary packages may need additional Buffer edge cases or codec aliases.
families.nextProof: Add canary coverage when a dependency upgrade introduces a new binary codec or Buffer edge case.

families.apiFamily: WebCrypto, Node crypto hashes, HMAC, PBKDF, random bytes, and timing-safe compare
families.acceptedSemantics: Current used crypto algorithms and WebCrypto paths are implemented in jsbridge. Unsupported algorithms should fail clearly instead of returning weak substitutes.
knownGaps: The inventory records crypto module use, not algorithm-level coverage.
Future provider or database packages may require additional ciphers or key formats.
families.nextProof: A future inventory revision should record algorithm coverage when new packages require crypto behavior beyond current tests.

families.apiFamily: fs, fs/promises, file streams, path, and sandboxed file access
families.acceptedSemantics: Filesystem behavior is sandbox-scoped and supports the file access patterns used by package tooling, parsers, storage adapters, and bundle dependencies.
knownGaps: Filesystem watchers and broad OS-level file descriptor semantics are not part of the current target.
Future parser canaries must use explicit fixture files rather than ambient host paths.
families.nextProof: Gate 7 parser canaries should prove in-memory and explicit fixture-file paths without expanding ambient filesystem authority.

families.apiFamily: fetch, URL, Headers, Request/Response, http, https, net, tls, dns, and WebSocket clients
families.owner: internal/jsbridge.Fetch, internal/jsbridge.NodeCompat, internal/jsbridge.Net, internal/jsbridge.DNS, internal/jsbridge.URL, and internal/jsbridge.WebSocketPoly
families.acceptedSemantics: fetch and WebSocket are primary network APIs. http.request/get and https.request/get are client-only compatibility subsets over fetch. net/tls/dns provide client behavior for database and provider SDKs. http.createServer, https.createServer, net.createServer, and tls.createServer are typed server-listener boundaries with suggested module/runtime owners.
knownGaps: http.createServer, https.createServer, net.createServer, tls.createServer, CONNECT, upgrade, raw sockets, and Node Agent pooling are unsupported boundaries.
HTTP client semantics are narrower than Node ClientRequest and IncomingMessage.
families.nextProof: Gate 7 should add local-service HTTP canaries for gaxios and node-fetch, including headers, bodies, abort, and compressed responses if practical. Server-listener support must remain outside this family until a module/runtime profile owns listener lifecycle and teardown.

families.apiFamily: zlib, gzip, deflate, inflate, and compression streams
families.acceptedSemantics: Compression helpers used by current database, document, and network packages are implemented in jsbridge.
knownGaps: Full Node compression stream parity and brotli policy are not fully expressed by the current inventory.
Optional native compression packages remain unsupported boundaries.
families.nextProof: Add compressed HTTP response coverage in the ecosystem canary suite if node-fetch or gaxios exercises it.

families.apiFamily: child_process, execa dynamic import, subprocess lifecycle, stdio, signals, and exit events
families.acceptedSemantics: Subprocess behavior is scoped through jsbridge Exec with resource accounting. execa is redirected to an explicit hook rather than arbitrary dynamic import behavior.
knownGaps: This is not an unmanaged Node process model.
Unsupported spawn options, inherited stdio, and platform-specific process controls must fail clearly.
families.nextProof: Keep subprocess resources in lifecycle checks and add typed diagnostics when packages request unsupported process options.

families.apiFamily: WebAssembly instantiate, modules, exports, memory, and validation
families.acceptedSemantics: WebAssembly.instantiate is backed by wazero for packages that ship deterministic WASM modules without WASI, threads, or native escape hatches.
knownGaps: WASI, WASM threads, host filesystem escape, and broad memory policy are not currently supported.
WASM package support is not yet proved by a non-Mastra ecosystem canary.
families.nextProof: Gate 7 should add an xxhash-wasm canary and assert module resources drain on close.

families.apiFamily: diagnostics_channel, perf_hooks, @opentelemetry/api, console, and tracing adjacency
families.acceptedSemantics: Mastra observability APIs and Brainkit tracing fixtures are covered separately. diagnostics_channel now provides real channel objects with subscribe/unsubscribe, synchronous publish, hasSubscribers, module-level subscribe/unsubscribe/hasSubscribers, and tracingChannel children backed by real channels. OTel remains import/shape compatibility only.
knownGaps: OTel active context/span propagation is not real.
perf_hooks exposes performance.now and minimal shape only.
families.nextProof: Promote further only when a tracing module owns OTel active span propagation and direct integration tests prove diagnostics-to-OTel context flow.

families.apiFamily: worker_threads, MessageChannel shape, transfer, shared memory, and parallel JS heaps
families.acceptedSemantics: Feature detection shape exists, but Worker construction is unsupported in QuickJS and throws a typed worker boundary diagnostic naming the future worker/sidecar owner.
knownGaps: No separate JS heap, message port, transfer, shared-memory, cancellation, or teardown model exists yet.
families.nextProof: A future worker profile must define separate JS heap ownership, message lifecycle, cancellation, transfer, and teardown proof before this can move beyond unsupported-boundary.

families.apiFamily: native addons, Node-API, optional native peers, platform bindings, and server-only external packages
families.owner: agent embed manifest externals and future resolver policy
families.acceptedSemantics: Optional native and external-only paths are not bundled into the QuickJS agent embed. Manifest and inventory rows carry boundaryClass and suggestedOwner metadata; runtime-reached dynamic requires throw typed boundary diagnostics when they cross these known unsupported imports. Pure JS, deterministic WASM, external-service, or sidecar paths must be chosen deliberately.
knownGaps: Current proof is mostly import/boundary classification, not runnable native behavior.
Sidecars are not designed for these paths yet.
families.nextProof: Gate 7 should add ecosystem canaries for optional native packages that prove the fallback path is pure JS, deterministic WASM, external service, or an explicit typed boundary.

families.apiFamily: version-scoped package compatibility patches and bundle rewrites
families.acceptedSemantics: Package patches are allowed only when version-scoped, manifest-declared, proof-backed, and paired with removal conditions.
knownGaps: Package patches should not become the default way to provide generic Node semantics.
Gemini Live remains disabled pending focused investigation.
families.nextProof: Gate 9 dependency upgrades must refresh package patch versions, expected markers, inventory, and capability rows.
